help.domains: A domain is a mail domain hosted directly on this server (e.g. example.com). Every user account belongs to exactly one domain. Adding a domain enables creating mailboxes of the form user@example.com.
help.virtualdomains: A virtual alias domain is a domain with no mailboxes of its own. Emails sent to any address under this domain are redirected to real mailboxes via alias rules. Each virtual alias domain can have one or more owners — accounts authorised to create and manage aliases under it.
help.externaldomains: Define the external mail providers users may connect accounts from.
help.application: Offers the webmail for installation as a desktop app: browsers then show an install icon in the address bar, and the app opens in its own window. The name and short name are what users see under the icon. Switching this off stops offering it — it does not uninstall the app for anyone who already installed it. Below: without a sending account, an appointment changed from a phone or Thunderbird does not notify the guests.

scheduling.title: Calendar invitation sending account
scheduling.intro: When an appointment with guests is changed from a phone or Thunderbird, the server sends the invitations with this account, in the organizer's name. Without it, those changes notify nobody.

deliveryReplies.title: Guests' replies at delivery
deliveryReplies.intro: The mail server can apply guests' replies the moment it delivers them, without waiting for the mail to be opened. Replies are then written without anyone having seen them. Opening the mail still applies a reply the delivery missed.
deliveryReplies.loadFailed: Could not load the delivery key.
deliveryReplies.noCall: No call received since the key was created
deliveryReplies.noKeyHint: Generate a key, copy it to the mail server, then enable.
deliveryReplies.dialogIntro: Copy this key now: it will not be shown again. Paste it into /etc/dovecot/calendar-reply.conf on the mail server, then enable the switch.
deliveryReplies.copyFailed: Could not copy: select the key and copy it by hand.
deliveryReplies.regenerateMessage: The mail server will be refused until its configuration holds the new key. Replies are still applied when the mail is opened meanwhile.
deliveryReplies.enabled: Replies are now applied at delivery.
deliveryReplies.disabled: Replies are now applied when the mail is opened.
deliveryReplies.deleteMessage: The key will be deleted and delivery-time replies disabled. The mail server's configuration will have to receive a new key.
